parts.title: Coffee Then And Now
parts.article:
(A) Coffee originated around the Red Sea, most probably in Ethiopia in Africa, and there are records of coffee cultivation in Yemen as early as the 6th century. By the 13th century, the growing, roasting and grinding of coffee to make a strong-flavoured infusion was widespread throughout the Arab world. News of the drink was brought to Europe by traders, but people there were at first wary of the new drink. However, Pope Clement the Eighth gave the drink his seal of approval after trying a cup for himself, and the trend quickly caught on. The 17th century saw the spread of coffee drinking throughout Europe. Coffee houses opened in Vienna, Paris and London, and they soon became the favourite meeting places of politicians, and were also known to attract artists of all kinds. By the 18th century, coffee production was well established in Java in Indonesia and also throughout the Caribbean. Coffee drinking continued to grow in popularity; one of the repercussions of the famous Boston Tea Party of 1773 was that the USA adopted coffee as its national beverage. Today, coffee is drunk around the world, though each nation has its own ways of preparing and serving it.

(B) Coffee is now grown in more than 50 countries, although production is not at all straightforward. Because it is vulnerable to frost, coffee can only be grown successfully between the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn. In addition, crop maintenance is labour intensive. The plants require constant care and attention, and in most areas the picking is carried out by hand.

(C) The ripe berry-like fruits which are harvested are called ‘cherries’. These ripen over a period of six to eight months and turn a deep red when ripe, which explains their name. Inside there are two green beans that have to be separated from the pulp and the skin, and dried. This process is known as curing, and it can be done by one of two methods. For the traditional ‘dry method’ of curing, the cherries are laid out in the sun until completely dry, and then the dried skins and pulp are removed from the beans. The ‘wet method’ is a more recent development and it is employed for high-quality hand-picked cherries. The outer, fleshy layer is removed, then the cherries are soaked and fermented, followed by washing and drying. Finally, the skins are removed by a machine, revealing the green beans.

(D) In both cases, the green beans are sorted, graded and packed for export. Roasting tends to be done in the country of import. The roasting process is necessary to reduce the acidity of the beans and to develop the aromatic oils, which give the coffee its aroma and flavour. Finally, grinding exposes a larger surface area to the water, ensuring optimum contact between the ground beans and the water, resulting in a more satisfying cup of coffee.

(E) The flavour, character and quality of coffee varies tremendously – not only between countries, but also between estates within the same country. The soil, altitude and climate are all factors that contribute to the character of the bean, thereby affecting the final taste. There are four varieties of coffee plant, but only two are sold on any commercial scale. The most important of these is coffea arabica, which grows on steep mountain slopes at high altitudes. The arabica bean produces coffee that is rich, aromatic and full of flavour, and it accounts for 70% of world coffee production. Coffee experts agree that the arabica bean is far superior in flavour to other types. The other main variety, coffea canephora, produces the coffee bean known as robusta.

(F) Grown on the lower slopes, where cultivation is easier, robusta beans have a higher caffeine content than arabica beans, and a rougher, almost earthy flavour that lacks delicacy and subtlety. It costs about half the price of arabica and is used in the cheaper blends of both fresh and instant coffee.

(G) There are three types of instant coffee. The cheapest is made from robusta beans that have been brewed into a concentrate. This is sprayed into a stream of hot air that instantly evaporates all moisture, leaving a fine powder. Some of the spray-dried powders undergo further heating to produce granular coffees; the better ones include some arabica beans. The best instant coffees are freeze-dried. For these, an arabica coffee concentrate is frozen and processed in a vacuum to produce crisp, dry particles of coffee.

(H) Caffeine is a stimulant that is present in coffee. It makes the nervous system more active, which is usually the desired effect. However, it can cause sleeplessness and therefore some consumers prefer to buy coffee without caffeine. Decaffeinated coffee is available in all the regular coffee forms: whole beans, ground or instant. Caffeine is removed by soaking the beans in water, or by the use of solvents or carbon dioxide. The latter is thought to be the best method as it does not affect the flavour and there is no residue. To qualify as decaffeinated, coffee must contain less than 0.9% caffeine.

Q2 The modern ‘wet method’ of curing is more efficient than the old ‘dry method’.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE

Q4 The roasting process improves both the smell and the taste of coffee.

Q5 Arabica coffee is harder to grow than robusta coffee.

  • A TRUE
  • B FALSE
  • C NOT GIVEN

Q6 The best instant coffee is a mix of arabica and robusta coffee.

reference:
Q1

解析 题目说咖啡果因为颜色被称为cherries，原文明确提到它们成熟时变成深红色，这就解释了名字的由来。

干扰 你可能会只看第13句没找到关于颜色的信息，但必须往后看第14句，里面“deep red”和“explains their name”完美对应了题目的因果关系。

句子 The ripe berry-like fruits which are harvested are called ‘cherries’. These ripen over a period of six to eight months and turn a deep red when ripe, which explains their name.

Q2

解析 原文虽然提到了传统的干法（dry method）和较新的湿法（wet method），但根本没有对比这两种方法谁效率更高（more efficient）。

干扰 你看到湿法是“more recent development”（较新发展）可能会自己脑补新方法一定效率更高，但做题绝不能用常识推断，没对比就是没提及。

句子 For the traditional ‘dry method’ of curing, the cherries are laid out in the sun until completely dry, and then the dried skins and pulp are removed from the beans. The ‘wet method’ is a more recent development and it is employed for high-quality hand-picked cherries.

Q3

解析 题目说生豆通常在出口前被烘焙，而原文明确说烘焙（Roasting）通常是在进口国（country of import）进行的。

干扰 你可能会把export（出口）和import（进口）看混，原文的“进口国烘焙”直接反驳了题目的“出口前烘焙”。

句子 In both cases, the green beans are sorted, graded and packed for export. Roasting tends to be done in the country of import.

Q4

解析 题目说烘焙过程改善了气味和味道，原文明确说烘焙能散发出芳香油，从而赋予咖啡香气（aroma）和风味（flavour）。

干扰 你可能不认识aroma和flavour，只要知道它们在原文中直接替换了题目里的smell和taste就能放心选TRUE。

句子 The roasting process is necessary to reduce the acidity of the beans and to develop the aromatic oils, which give the coffee its aroma and flavour.

Q5

解析 原文说robusta种在较低的山坡上，那里的种植更容易（cultivation is easier），直接反向说明了另一种豆子arabica更难种植。

干扰 你没在原文找到“harder”可能会不敢选，但“A种植更容易”等同于“B种植更难”，这是非常典型的反向替换。

句子 The other main variety, coffea canephora, produces the coffee bean known as robusta. Grown on the lower slopes, where cultivation is easier, robusta beans have a higher caffeine content than arabica beans, and a rougher, almost earthy flavour that lacks delicacy and subtlety.

Q6

解析 题目说最好的速溶咖啡是这两种豆子混合的，但原文明确指出最好的速溶咖啡只用了阿拉比卡咖啡浓缩液（an arabica coffee concentrate）。

干扰 你可能看到前面第37句提到了混合豆子，但那是“better ones”（较好的），而题目问的是“best”（最好的），定位要精准。

句子 The best instant coffees are freeze-dried. For these, an arabica coffee concentrate is frozen and processed in a vacuum to produce crisp, dry particles of coffee.

Q7

解析 题目在找表明也门种咖啡的“早期某物”，原文直接给出了早在6世纪就有在也门种植咖啡的记录（records）。

干扰 你可能会把cultivation填进去，但空格前面的修饰词是early，对应原文的“as early as”，真正发出“表明”这个动作的主体是records。

句子 Coffee originated around the Red Sea, most probably in Ethiopia in Africa, and there are records of coffee cultivation in Yemen as early as the 6th century.

Q8

解析 题目问欧洲人最初是从谁那里听说咖啡的，原文直接说消息是由商人（traders）带到欧洲的。

干扰 你可能会死抠表示“听”的动词，但原文用了被动语态“被...带到欧洲”，只要认准“by”后面的动作发出者traders就行。

句子 News of the drink was brought to Europe by traders, but people there were at first wary of the new drink.

Q9

解析 题目问在教皇喝了之后，咖啡在欧洲变成了一种什么，原文指出教皇认可后，这种趋势（trend）迅速流行了起来。

干扰 你可能会把caught填进去，但空格前有个“a”，必须填一个单数名词，trend（趋势）刚好契合语法和句意。

句子 However, Pope Clement the Eighth gave the drink his seal of approval after trying a cup for himself, and the trend quickly caught on.

Q10

解析 题目列举了画家和另一类人在咖啡馆聚会，原文中明确提到了咖啡馆成了政治家（politicians）最喜欢的聚会场所。

干扰 你可能会想填artists，但题目里的painters（画家）已经是artists的具体举例了，所以要填前面并列的另一类人politicians。

句子 Coffee houses opened in Vienna, Paris and London, and they soon became the favourite meeting places of politicians, and were also known to attract artists of all kinds.

Q11

解析 题目问在热带种咖啡是为了避免什么造成的损害，原文说它容易受到霜冻（frost）的伤害，所以只能在热带种植。

干扰 你可能不认识vulnerable（易受伤害的）这个词，它直接替换了题目的“damage caused by”，找到这个替换逻辑就能直接锁定frost。

句子 Because it is vulnerable to frost, coffee can only be grown successfully between the Tropics of Cancer and Capricorn.

Q12

解析 题目问咖啡种植中什么通常是手工（manually）完成的，原文明确说在大多数地区，采摘（picking）是由手工（by hand）进行的。

干扰 你可能没有立刻发现manually和by hand的同义替换关系，只要看出这个替换，就能立马找到它们前面的动作词picking。

句子 The plants require constant care and attention, and in most areas the picking is carried out by hand.

Q13

解析 题目问用二氧化碳能保持咖啡的什么，原文指出用二氧化碳最好，因为它不会影响风味（flavour）。

干扰 你如果只看第45句会不知道“The latter”指代什么，必须向前看第44句确认它指的是二氧化碳，然后用“does not affect”替换“maintains”就能锁定flavour。

句子 Caffeine is removed by soaking the beans in water, or by the use of solvents or carbon dioxide. The latter is thought to be the best method as it does not affect the flavour and there is no residue.
